title: Harness Lab
blurb: Curated tips and methods that make this Field Brief / EM fleet stronger — Grok bots, Mac CLIs, Obsidian vault, routines, and launch standards. Keep only what we can apply; not generic AI news.

entries.title: Ruttla — deterministic quality gate: every rule must fail its broken probe and pass its healthy one, and exit 2 means nothing was measured
entries.why: Local quality gate that turns a proven failure into an executable rule: a rule must fail its broken probe and pass its healthy probe, and ruttla --self-test re-runs both. The exit code is a contract: 0 measured with no blocking finding, 1 a blocking finding, 2 nothing was measured (the README says not a success), 3 a runner, input, config or plugin error. Without its engine the declarative rules report as unmeasured, never green, and platforms with no rule pack are listed instead of passing. The README warns that ruttla . | head reports head's status, so capture the code before filtering. --format agent prints one line per finding with a FIX: hint; scans use no LLM or network and never execute target code. Fit: it puts our negative-claim rule and code decides done into an exit code a wrapper can test, and its two-probe test is an admission rule for checks we add. Caveats: 0.1.0.dev0 public preview; rule messages are currently in German; the quick install pipes a script to sh; 0 stars, Apache-2.0, created 2026-09-18; README-verified, not installed or run. Reference only; any live-seat install, hook, or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: sandbox-run — verify in a detached worktree overlaid by manifest copy, then check the main tree's VCS state stayed byte-identical
entries.why: Runs build, test or lint commands in a detached git worktree (or jj workspace) in a temp directory, not the live checkout. Uncommitted files are overlaid by manifest copy, never patch-apply, hardlink or symlink, so writes cannot leak back, and cache directories such as target/ and node_modules/ are left out, so a pass comes from a clean rebuild and catches a forgotten new file the way CI would. Timeouts kill the whole process group. The isolation.integrity gate checks that the main tree's VCS state is byte-identical before and after (failure exits 2). By default, sandbox.clean marks a run that changed the snapshot as polluted, and runs are logged to the append-only .sandbox-run/runs.jsonl. Fit: our wrapper fails a push-required kick on a dirty tree (no-exit-while-waiting), and the README's first problem is build artifacts mixing into the change set; it isolates only the verify step. Caveats: the ledger is the one file it writes in the main tree, so .sandbox-run/ needs a .gitignore line; a large project's first run rebuilds caches slowly; Rust CLI; 0 stars, MIT, created 2026-08-20; README-verified, not installed or run. Reference only; any live-seat install, hook, or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: claude-tmux — tmux window marks for working, done with a background command still running, waiting on you, and a prompt cache about to go cold
entries.why: tmux plugin that names each Claude Code window after its session and puts a state mark where the colon was: ◐ ◓ ◑ ◒ turning while it works, ◌ when it is done but a command it started in the background still runs, ◉ when it is your move, and ◉ on darker green on a permission prompt or dialog. It also times the prompt cache from the last 128 KB of each transcript: the name changes color at 30, 20 and 10 minutes left and the mark flashes ❄ for the last 5 (on a one-hour cache; the points scale on a five-minute one). The state is also a tmux format variable, @claude_state. Fit: our Mac CLI jobs already run in tmux under grok-tmux-run, ◌ is the state behind no-exit-while-waiting, and the cache marks show the TTL that cachebeat and cache-live-control manage; Gate Inbox is an adjacent tmux waiting-state board. Caveats: Claude Code only, read from a session registry under ~/.claude/sessions that the README calls undocumented (a changed format shows nothing, not a wrong mark); the README is silent on headless claude -p runs; needs tmux 3.2+ and jq; the author says Claude wrote almost all of the code; writes nothing to disk, no network calls; 0 stars, MIT, created 2026-09-27; README-verified, not installed or run. Reference only; any live-seat install, hook, or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: effortless — a Jev or Haiku judge picks reasoning effort for each prompt, plus a prompt-cache countdown with one-click Compact
entries.why: Claude Code mod where a judge picks reasoning effort per prompt: TypeSafe Jev when a key is set (about 0.25 s, TYPESAFE_API_KEY), else Haiku on your own Claude login (about 1 s), falling back to Haiku on error or past 3 s; setting effort by hand turns Auto off. A footer countdown shows the prompt cache's time left and offers Compact once it is cold. Its reported version 1.5.1 benchmark (73 cases, 20 held out) puts Jev at 99% against 51% for always-high, which the README says measures effort choice, not cost or answer quality; its cost note says Auto saves a lot against a high default (a median xhigh prompt cost about three times a medium one) and a few percent against medium. Fit: a Jev effort-routing candidate, with the constant baselines our Jev rule asks for; a trial must square it with the max-effort defaults referenced in the pack's 2026-09-24 lock, and the README does not say how the mod sets effort. Caveats: Auto pauses on Fable 5.1; the terminal may need CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 in settings; a live-seat install needs the mod precondition (written load order, named first loader, owner, read before install); 0 stars, MIT, created 2026-10-06; README-verified, not installed or run. Reference only; any live-seat install, hook, or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: proof-of-done — Stop hook that blocks a tests-pass, build or deploy claim unless the transcript shows the command ran after the last relevant edit and succeeded
entries.why: Claude Code plugin whose Stop hook checks specific claims (tests pass, build succeeds, lint or types clean, fixed, verified, deployed) against the session's own transcript: the latest matching foreground Bash command after the last relevant edit decides. Failed, empty and background-only runs do not count; masked runs (| tail, || true) are inconclusive when their output shows no success line, and a block ends with a Run: line naming the command. It makes no network or model call, fails open, caps itself at 2 blocks in a row, honors #skip-proof only from the human, and partly undoes the session's own attempts to switch it off; an audit command replays past transcripts. On a synthetic held-out set (one author wrote detector and fixtures, the README notes) the gate scores 98.2% precision and 82.1% recall, and 1.0% of turns without an unsupported claim were falsely blocked. Fit: code decides done and the receipt's VERIFIED field, enforced at the stop; unlike POAW in the 10-05 Titan card it never asks the destination. Caveats: English keywords only, so phrasings like Types check go unchecked; transcript format pinned to Claude Code 2.1.281; headless claude -p behavior not verified here; 0 stars, Apache-2.0, created 2026-09-28; README-verified, not installed or run. Reference only; any live-seat install, hook, or settings change needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: claude-code-dispatch — hook-enforced model/effort routing for subagents, an orchestrator write-deny, and a replay benchmark against the dumbest baseline
entries.why: PreToolUse hooks that print one dispatch line per subagent launch (model, effort, type, plan usage, job), stop model-less dispatches from silently inheriting the parent's premium model, ask before premium or high-stakes-on-cheap launches, and log every launch to JSONL. A separate gate denies code Edit/Write/Bash in the orchestrator session so it must brief a worker (plans and scratch stay writable, workers exempt), a non-blocking tripwire lists code a parent changed anyway via node -e or a script, and the escape hatch lasts one turn only. Rule: raise effort before tier; stakes never downshift, even when usage is red. Its replay benchmark scores routers on your own dispatch history against the dumbest baseline: a keyword rule (89%) beat an LLM classifier (84%). Turns our prose rules (no Grok bot writes code; per-seat max effort) into something that denies, and matches the Jev dumb-baseline lock. Caveats: 0 stars, MIT, single-day repo, macOS untested and the usage snapshot reads UNKNOWN there (Keychain token); the orchestrator gate is inert unless its model regex matches our orchestrator; README-verified, not installed or run. Shadow-first; a live-seat deny gate needs Haiyuan. Patterns over existing seats, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: Titan Receipts + POAW — a receipt only counts if the party it describes can't verify it, and a claim that is only local is not evidence
entries.why: Titan gives every commit a hash-chained, HMAC-signed receipt (model, Claude Code version, session, file and diff hashes), verifiable offline. Its CI check runs its own pinned verifier, never the copy committed in the repo under audit, because the party who could alter receipts also controls a vendored verifier; the escape hatch warns that the result is then self-reported. /verify-chain ends with an ANCHOR count of untracked, uncommitted or unpushed receipts, a keyless clone says SIGNATURES NOT CHECKED and exits 2, and the README spells out what a receipt proves and what it doesn't. POAW / qed-proof-core (https://github.com/Nuraveda/qed-proof-core) adds the destination check: when an agent claims a push, the node asks GitHub and signs a pass or Failed receipt into an append-only Merkle log. Fits our gap-not-zero and VERIFIED-means-ran receipt locks, which today are self-administered, and the no-exit-while-waiting push rule. Caveats: Titan 1 star, MIT, HMAC is a shared secret; POAW 3 stars, Apache-2.0 spec plus AGPL-3.0 node, so patterns only and copy nothing, and it was read at headline level; README-verified, not run. Documentation pattern, no new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: bastionfuse — containment that never reads text: honeytokens, decoys, taint-then-egress, and a sticky per-session fuse
entries.why: Starts from the case we never write down, that the model itself is the attacker, so it relies only on controls outside the LLM. It plants honeytokens, decoy files and decoy MCP tools, matches tokens in call inputs and in results across common encodings, and taints a session that reads a decoy; after that, any data-capable call trips the fuse. That catches curl -d @.env.backup even though the secret never appears in the arguments. Trips are sticky and per session, a bounded trace is kept, the guard protects its own state and settings, and the state path is baked into the hook. Rollout: operator-written rules enforce from day one, while built-in budgets only log 'would trip' until real sessions are reviewed, which is a clean statement of our shadow-to-active ladder. Fills a gap next to coding-agent-guardrails and Preflight, which prevent or declare but have no canary. Caveats are the README's own: tamper-evident, not tamper-proof, against a same-user agent; a hook that can't start fails open; /clear or deleting state resets it; shell egress detection is word-based; about 250 ms per tool call; 0 stars, MIT, created the day it was collected; README-verified, not run. Reference only; any live-seat hook needs Haiyuan. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: cache-live-control — prompt-cache TTL as a per-chat decision, with the agent's wait and delegation rule priced against it
entries.why: Claude Code plugin whose /cache command switches the main-chat and subagent TTLs separately, mid-session, at no cost. It publishes the TTL source-precedence table (FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M down to automatic: 1h on a subscription, 5m on an API key or cloud provider) and notes that subagents default to 5m even when the main chat is on 1h. Its new idea is a priced-wait rule: on a 1h cache, delegate anything past roughly 30 tool calls and wait, because waiting is free and writes cost 2x; on 5m, work directly and keep each wait under 4 minutes. It also names the transcript fields that make cache claims checkable (message.usage.cache_creation ephemeral_5m / ephemeral_1h input tokens, with subagent messages under subagents/), and reports 11 of 12 warm TTL switches kept the cache. Adds the missing decision to our cache lane (cachebeat, cache-keepalive, contextscope, stable-context-first measure or reorder; none picks the TTL). Caveats: built on early-access function hooks; it can't see the plan, so it assumes the longer TTL; the measurement is the author's own 12 runs; 1 star, MIT; README-verified, not installed. Doc pattern now; a live-seat install needs the mod precondition (written load order, named first loader, owner, read before install). No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: token-weather-usage — usage limits shown against elapsed time, with the cause of every cache miss named
entries.why: One-band Claude Code mod that shows the 5h and 7d limits as a share of the account limit with the gap against elapsed time hatched: green while usage doesn't run ahead of the clock, yellow beyond, red when more than 15 points ahead or past 90%. Windows that already reset stay hidden until the next reading, and the latest reading is shared across every session open on the machine. The cache pill shows the share read from cache and the time left before it lapses, and on a miss it names the cause (model changed, lapsed, start changed). Cost is labelled as an API-price equivalent on a subscription, not a bill. It makes no network calls. Gives our usage dashboard its missing axis: Agent Limit Watchdog and agent-runway compare a bare percentage, so 74% with 24 minutes left looks the same as 74% with two hours left. A pacing column and miss-cause labels can come from data we already collect, with nothing installed. Caveats: a mod is unsandboxed code with Claude Code's own access, so installing it on a live seat needs the mod precondition; the thresholds are the author's defaults, not measured; the cache lifetime is inferred from traffic; 3 stars, Apache-2.0; README-verified, not run. No new seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: loupe — review envelopes bound to commit SHAs, fingerprinted findings, and circuit breakers that stop non-converging rounds
entries.why: Deterministic, agent-neutral review plumbing with no model inside: request, verdict, disposition and authorization envelopes each bound to a commit SHA; findings fingerprinted with alias lineage so they can't quietly change between rounds; an append-only ledger; and circuit breakers (repetition, stale, no-progress, unverifiable, budget, orphan) that block the next handoff until a human records a decision. A human carries every leg. Fits our verdict-on-head-SHA rule, finetooth-style fingerprints and the human gate, and gives a machine form of 'reviewer loops must terminate'. Caveats: 0 stars, MIT, Python 3.15.x pinned, published-not-developed (issues only); adds relay latency; README-verified, not installed or run. Patterns/reference over existing seats, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: corralai — critic must differ from writer, unreproduced review claims are demoted, mutation kill-rate measures test adequacy (patterns only)
entries.why: Auditing engine that refuses to grade its own work. certify plants goal-violating faults and runs your own suite against each one, so the kill-rate is measured, not self-reported, and 'zero proven gaps means nothing was proven'. review uses a decorrelated adversary: every claim ships a script it runs, unreproduced claims are demoted on the record, and the run refuses to start if the critic matches the writer. Fits our implementer-not-reviewer and blind dual-LGTM rule (refuse, not just discourage), our negative-claim rule, and mutation-based test adequacy. Its measured cross-model blind-spot overlap (Jaccard 0.750 over 13 survivors, author-reported) is worth reading before any multi-seat review fan-out. Caveats: Elastic-2.0, so patterns only, do not vendor or run as a hosted service; 2 stars; certify needs a provider key, Go toolchain and sandbox time; README-verified, not run. No Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: delivery-harness — autonomy per task class with an error budget, hash-locked harness engine, and tests run at the base version
entries.why: Verifiable delivery harness whose engine is vendored per project and hash-locked (verify fails on drift; changes only through a reviewable upgrade PR). Checks that check themselves: Defect-trailer fixes must fail before and pass after, existing tests run at the base version so the agent can't weaken them, past incidents are replayed, and quality baselines only move one way. Risk is routed R0 to R3 from the paths touched, not author claims, and autonomy is granted per task class with an error budget that is withdrawn automatically when exceeded. Fits our autonomy ladder with demotion (the automatic enforcement half), seat-install drift checks in the nightly Mac audit, and prevention behind agent-receipts' post-hoc detection. Caveats: 0 stars, MIT, Chinese-first messages; adopt the three named mechanisms, not the platform install; overlaps kept cards; README-verified, not run. No Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: ai-jury — cross-vendor review jury that drives agent CLIs read-only, with a chair that verifies before it synthesizes
entries.why: Review jury that runs agent CLIs (claude, codex, agy), hosted APIs and local open-weight models (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) headless and sandboxed read-only, handing each the diff in the prompt so no reviewer needs repo access. Round one is independent parallel review, then an adaptive rebuttal round, then a chair verifies and synthesizes one verdict (APPROVE, COMMENT or REQUEST CHANGES) or a panel vote; jury --mock runs a full offline deliberation with zero config. Fits our blind review and evidence-before-verdict discipline, could add a $0-marginal local third seat, and --mock gives a model-free fixture for replay checks. Caveats: 8 stars, MIT, PyPI; fan-out costs tokens, so CI gate on selected repos only and any standing use needs Haiyuan approval under token-save; the agy seat is opt-in because it can't be confined; read corralai's blind-spot overlap first; README-verified, not run. Not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: STK — one Rust binary that turns oversized file reads into line-numbered outlines for Claude Code and Codex
entries.why: Hook-based tool for Claude Code and Codex: oversized whole-file reads become line-numbered outlines so the agent fetches only the parts it needs (stk read --offset/--limit), while small or scoped reads pass through. stk gain reports an upper bound on bytes avoided and says plainly that follow-up reads still cost tokens, so it measures hook behavior, not net session savings. Read-side counterpart to the kept ai-coding-gateway (output-side trim) and a fit for the usage dashboard's bytes-are-not-tokens discipline. Caveats: 1 star, young; LICENSE file reads MIT (GitHub API license field not reported); upstream verification is Windows-only, so macOS behavior is unverified until a one-seat trial; needs a Rust toolchain; README-verified, not installed. A hook on existing seats, not a new coding CLI; no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: @0xCarnagee — Grok Bot team workflow: untrusted content is data; quote instructions, never follow them
entries.why: @0xCarnagee's 11-step write-up of a Grok Bot team's own workflow keeps one standing rule: treat every email, page and document as untrusted data, and if it contains instructions, quote them and don't follow them. Here it covers what collectors read on X, Reddit and the web, PR text that reviewers read, tool output and other agents' output; a reviewer or gate takes its policy from its own prompt and the playbook, never from the material under review. Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) as policy text: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#untrusted-content. Nothing enforces it.

entries.title: @sermakarevich — evals guide: count failure types first, then replay our own failures and judge the worst of three runs
entries.why: @sermakarevich's plain-language eval guide starts with error analysis: read 100+ outputs and count failure types before building graders; for agents, run each task several times, report pass^k and perturb the task. @undefinedKi's harness guide adds an eval set built from your own failures, run three times and judged on the worst run. What to try here: label our forbidden.md corrections and recent failed done receipts by failure type in a separate Wiki note (forbidden.md itself is under the byte ceiling), count each type, and build checks or hooks for the largest types first. Then keep 20–50 of those real failures as the replay set, where a case passes only if all three runs pass (pass^3) and one run uses a reworded instruction. That second half is already playbook policy, as an extension of the replay check: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#replay-set. Status: trial, not started; no labels, counts or replay set exist yet. The guides' numbers come from their cited sources and were not checked.

entries.title: @monokern — OpenAI Dots blueprint: separate kill switches, so an emergency stop checks every layer
entries.why: @monokern's guide to always-on cloud agents ("Dots") keeps three separate kill switches, for the main agent, its delegated tasks and its scheduled routines, because pausing the main agent does not cancel the others. Here a stop is checked on five layers: the bot, its routines, its in-flight delegated tasks or tmux jobs, its open kick-ledger rows and any active Jev gate. Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) as a verification list next to the weekly kill review: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#emergency-stop. Stopping a bot stays a RED action that needs Haiyuan's approval; the list is not permission. The guide's product and pricing claims are the author's and were not checked.

entries.title: @heyang_zhou — Comma's Salix event loops: dedupe key, wake budget, auto-pause with a recorded reason
entries.why: Comma's Salix lets an agent write tiny sandboxed watcher programs ("Loops") that run outside the model, call Jev for cheap typed decisions on each event, and wake the main agent only when needed. Each wake carries a dedupe key and a budget (6 per 10 minutes); a Loop over budget auto-pauses with a reason. What to try here: give every bot-to-bot wake, kick re-wake or catch-up a stable key so a redelivery fires once; cap wakes per routine per window, and pause a routine that sits at the cap, with the reason recorded and reported; add a deterministic no-op pre-screen (for example, zero new URLs after dedupe skips the model run); and keep @0xCarnagee's rule that silence is a valid result, so a run never manufactures an update. First trial: a dedupe key on the Coding EM kick ledger, where the 2026-09-24 room kick the heartbeat never read and the overlap between re-wakes and heartbeats are the exposure. Status: trial, not started. Salix benchmarks are the author's and were not checked.

entries.title: @sermakarevich — evals guide: re-audit gates and rules when a model or version in the path changes
entries.why: @sermakarevich's eval guide says to calibrate a cheap gate once against ground truth and re-audit it when the model, the judge or the domain changes. What to try here: when a model or version in the path changes (Opus 5.5, Astra, Jev 1.13, a Mac CLI update), re-run the Jev shadow report and the replay set, and review whether each lint, hook or prompt rule still earns its place; delete rules that a better model made pointless. Where it applies: Jev gates checked against the constant baseline, and the rules under the resident-policy byte ceiling. The byte ceiling and the Monday kill review exist, but nothing fires on a model change, so calibrated gates can go stale without anyone noticing. Status: backlog; the first real use is the next model or CLI version change. The guide's numbers come from its cited sources and were not checked.

entries.title: Tetral (Yang Li) — The Next Scaling Problem: a timeout does not prove the old worker stopped
entries.why: Yang Li's post on Tetral, an open-source alpha cloud-agent runtime, keeps the agent replaceable and commits every transition before the action is dispatched. It notes that a timeout does not prove the old worker stopped, so a fencing token keeps a stale worker from acting; Comma's Salix gives each Loop a fence value for the same reason. What to try here: grok-tmux-watchdog resumes the same session when its log goes stale (~540s), and the resumed run should start only after the old process is confirmed dead. Whether the watchdog kills the old process before it resumes is not verified; its code has not been read for this. Status: trial; the first step is to read that code. Tetral says placement, backpressure and multi-node recovery are not yet proven.

entries.title: @undefinedKi — six harness decisions: when almost every prompt is approved, use a boundary instead
entries.why: @undefinedKi's six-decision harness guide prefers OS-level write and network boundaries to approval prompts, citing a 93% prompt approval rate and 84% fewer prompts after sandboxing; both are the author's second-hand numbers and were not verified. Here: track how often Haiyuan approves each category in the decision queue, and propose a category approved more than about 90% of the time for GREEN/YELLOW policy or a boundary instead of a prompt. Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) as policy text under the decision queue: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#approval-rate.

entries.title: @Michaelzsguo — Poteto x Matt Pocock interview summary: batch-triage findings and fix common causes
entries.why: A Chinese summary by @Michaelzsguo of the Poteto x Matt Pocock interview: findings are appended to a doc and reviewed in a batch days later to find common causes; a coordinator agent groups related reports before executors run; and human review is strict spot-checking that changes the environment, not review of each PR. What to try here: the nightly Mac harness audit and other audit agents append findings to one log instead of fixing each one; a weekly review clusters them and fixes the root cause; and related inbound reports are grouped before a Mac CLI is kicked. Status: backlog. Caveats: only the summary was read, not the interview; the 2,500 PRs are self-reported and mostly maintenance work.

entries.title: Tetral (Yang Li) — admit work to the shared workspace only after review: accepted vs draft vault notes
entries.why: Yang Li's Tetral post says work enters the shared workspace only after other agents challenge its conclusions and evidence. The lesson for us is memory admission: only reviewed artifacts should change what future agents trust; chat coordinates, accepted notes compound. Today every Hunt and Wiki note in the vault reads as truth, with no accepted-vs-draft state. What to try here: give vault notes a draft or accepted state, and have agents treat draft notes as leads to check, not facts. Status: backlog; no format chosen and no note changed. Tetral is an alpha runtime by its own account.

entries.title: @undefinedKi — six harness decisions: structured tool errors, lazily loaded and pruned tool menus
entries.why: @undefinedKi's six-decision harness guide asks for structured error messages from tools, tools loaded lazily, and unused tools pruned from the menu. What to try here: our own helpers (jev-route, receipt, vault-note, grok-tmux-*) return errors that name the field, the valid value and the next step, and MCP tool descriptions stay on disk until a task needs them. Status: backlog; no helper has been changed. The guide's statistics are cited second-hand and were not checked.

entries.title: @sermakarevich — evals guide: give completion_check the evidence, not the narrative; name the reviewer model
entries.why: @sermakarevich's eval guide says a judge should get binary questions with evidence and be checked against human labels, and reports that a judge which saw only the chat did no better than chance. What to try here: feed Jev completion_check the evidence (exit codes, URLs, the done receipt) instead of the agent's own account, and record the reviewer model and version in the VERDICT line so a verdict can be re-audited after a model change. Status: backlog; completion_check stays shadow and advisory, and code decides done still rules. The guide's numbers come from its cited sources and were not checked.

entries.title: @sermakarevich — evals guide: check citations claim by claim, accept only above a confidence threshold
entries.why: @sermakarevich's eval guide cites a typed judge (Jev) and small claim-support detectors. What to try here: in the Field Brief citation step, ask one typed question per claim (is it supported by this excerpt?), answered by Jev or a small detector, and accept the claim only above a confidence threshold. First trial: shadow only, inside the existing research_check gate, which logs and never blocks. Status: trial, not started; no threshold chosen. The guide's numbers come from its cited sources and were not checked.

entries.title: @poteto — most used prompt: restate my goals and the problem before you start
entries.why: A one-sentence post from @poteto quoting a most used prompt: "restate in your own words what you think my goals are and what the problem I'm trying to solve is." No linked content. Here: before a non-trivial task the agent restates the goal and the problem, and the restatement is compared with the intent before work starts. Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) as one line in Light Mission DoD: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#intake-restatement.

entries.title: @sermakarevich — evals guide: state the detection floor; three runs only catch large regressions
entries.why: @sermakarevich's eval guide asks for paired comparisons with error bars and a stated detection floor. Here: three runs only catch large regressions, and three clean runs do not show that a smaller regression is absent, so a promotion note says so and lists every case that got worse, even when all three runs passed. Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) as a caveat on Three-Run Proof: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#detection-floor. The guide's numbers come from its cited sources and were not checked.

entries.title: @monokern — OpenAI Dots blueprint: five tests before creating a new bot
entries.why: @monokern's Dots guide runs five tests before an always-on agent is created: a specific goal, its own sources, a working style, an approval boundary and a cadence. Here they become a five-test charter for a new bot, with cadence read as its trigger (a schedule or an event). Also in the playbook since 2026-10-04 (Haiyuan-approved) in How to extend the team: https://caohy1988.github.io/research/harness/#five-test-charter. entries.title: @karpathy — make agent output easy to understand: short controlled-language reports for oversight

entries.title: stingray — Claude Code / Codex Stop hook for half-done turns and unbacked wait promises

Judgements go to TypeSafe Jev; local count backs shape 3; fixed stderr nudge offers finish / launch a poll / name the blocker. Fails open (exit 0) on every error path so a broken hook never grants less friction. Also ships wrong_language and STINGRAY_SHADOW (log-only, never blocks). Caveat: without a Jev API key the checks skip (does nothing). Enforces no-exit-while-waiting mechanically for Coding EM seats. Claude Code plugin + Codex marketplace plugin; MIT. Not a new coding-CLI seat, no Herdr. Lab card; appliedToPlaybook false.

entries.title: cachebeat — inactivity-triggered prompt-cache heartbeat (Claude Code)

entries.title: crossagent — dual-agent tmux review with AGREE/ESCALATE/UNPARSED verdicts
entries.why: MCP server (npm crossagent-mcp) that pairs two coding agents in adjacent tmux panes — one drives, the other reviews. Every plan/diff passes through the peer; the reply always ends in a machine-parseable `VERDICT: <word>` with fixed vocabulary: AGREE / ADJUST / OBJECT / ESCALATE / UNPARSED. tmux is the only transport (no network, no shared file, no socket); briefing clears the peer's conversation so the reviewer is genuinely fresh. Gives blind dual-LGTM (Astra+Fable) an interface: today reviewers can return prose we adjudicate by reading; ESCALATE is "only the human can call it" (silent-misroute rule in mechanical form) and UNPARSED detects a non-verdict instead of treating it as assent (retry ceiling schema×1). Adopt the verdict contract as prose/checklist first; installing the MCP is optional/later. Requires Node 22+, tmux, Claude Code or Codex CLI. MIT. In playbook (2026-09-27, Haiyuan-approved) as the review verdict line (#review-verdict-line): VERDICT: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | ESCALATE @ head SHA; a missing line is UNPARSED and never an LGTM. MCP not installed.

Briefs state the outcome + observable criteria, not line-by-line steps ("the model owns the path; the ledger owns the destination"). Also ships max vs low-cost routing profiles (frontier for judgment, cheaper models for research/implementation), which mirrors our Opus-default / Kimi-fallback / flash-collect split. entries.title: agent-evals — record once, replay offline; gate on pass rate, cost p95, trajectory, calibrated judge
entries.why: Eval harness that records model calls once and replays them offline (no key, no network, runs in CI), then gates on pass rate, cost p95 (not mean), latency, and trajectory (catches right-answer-wrong-path, e.g. a refund that skips the lookup), with the LLM judge calibrated against human labels (agreement, Cohen's kappa, false passes, order/length bias). Shape for the rari promotion gate + Three-Run Proof trial: replay keeps repeat runs at $0, trajectory checks catch skipped steps, and any Jev/LLM gate promoted from shadow should report kappa + false passes, not a bare score. Caveat from its own README: the same suite scored 92% on replay but 28–44% live (mostly brittle exact-substring asserts), so replay is a regression guard, not proof of live quality. Small, new repo (created 09-23): borrow the pattern, don't add a dependency. In playbook (2026-09-25, Haiyuan-approved) as a light replay regression check inside Three-Run Proof, before skill/prompt promotion or Jev shadow→active; live Three-Run Proof stays the bar.

In playbook §5/§12/§16 + checklist.
